reason: Jamku charges only ₹6,500 a year, so paying ₹12,990 upfront for Docketra feels twice as expensive for our 3 to 5 person firm without proving its value first. While article clerks taking client data home on personal laptops gives me anxiety, in a normal week outside filing panic I would only test the free pilot before paying double what established tools charge.
objection: Jamku charges only ₹6,500 a year—why is Docketra more expensive, and does the Trainee Laptop Shield truly stop clerks from downloading client data to personal laptops?
would_change_my_mind: Pricing closer to Jamku around ₹7,000 to ₹8,000 a year, or concrete proof during the free pilot that the Trainee Laptop Shield completely blocks file downloads and eliminates my peer-review panic.
